output:
(1) Why flaky: Both score quality 0.92. Python’s sorted is stable, so ties keep results order. run_bench appends from a thread pool as each call returns, so that order is a finish-time race. ranked[0] is whichever call completed first among ties—not a quality winner.

(2) Local vs CI: Quiet local (and solo re-run) timing almost always yields the same finisher first. CI load/jitter flips completion order ~1/5, so the name assertion fails intermittently; re-running alone often restores the lucky order.

(3) Fix: deterministic tie-break, e.g. sorted(results, key=lambda r: (-r["quality"], r["model"])), or assert the tied top set—not one model after quality-only sort.

Test bug (underspecified ties), not a product bug unless ranking claims a total order without a tie-break.

judgeDetail.rationale: Nails tie + stable-sort + thread-completion-order mechanism, correct CI-vs-local reasoning, deterministic secondary-key fix, and correctly frames it as a test bug — only minor prose compression keeps it from flawless.
